Prepared: August 8, 2026 · Supersedes the earlier B2B/website-builder audit, which you've confirmed doesn't apply.

## What I actually looked at

Logged in as your account, I went through: Square (main feed + daily debate prompt), Live (audio/video debate rooms), all six Arenas (Sports, Politics, Entertainment, News, Spirituality, Startups), Explore/search, Communities, your own profile, one live room in detail, and a mobile-width (390px) view. ## 1. One-sentence verdict

**Verdict:** BaratX has one genuinely differentiated mechanic (live, sided debate rooms) buried under a product that currently reads as mostly empty and mostly auto-generated, so it's differentiated on paper but not yet credible or converting in practice.

Scores (out of 10):

| Dimension | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Positioning | 5/10 | "India's public square" + debate framing is a real angle, distinct from a generic feed — but it's not reinforced consistently (see Arenas vs. Communities overlap below) |
| Design | 6/10 | Clean, modern, legible UI on desktop; a real mobile bug (see #4) knocks this down |
| Clarity | 5/10 | The core action ("answer today's question," "pick a side") is clear in isolation; the overall structure (Square vs. Live vs. Arenas vs. Communities — four sections that overlap heavily) is not |
| Trust | 2/10 | Nearly every debate, room, and community shows 0 replies / 0 takes / 1–4 members; the content that exists is dominated by an official account reformatting news headlines, not real users debating |
| Conversion (activation/engagement) | 2/10 | I could not find a single thread, room, or community with visible organic back-and-forth — the core loop hasn't been shown to work yet, at least not on what's visible to this account |
| Scalability (network effects/growth) | 4/10 | The "Founding ₹150" creator incentive and topic-tag taxonomy (e.g., 48 tags under Startups alone) are real scaffolding for growth — but they're pointed at 6+ diffuse categories at once instead of one dense community |

---

## 2. Five-second test

**What's on screen for you today:** "Today's Square: College prepared you for work — true or false? Defend it." with a "Post your take" prompt, topic pills up top (Sports/Politics/Entertainment/News/Spirituality/Startups), and a floating "+" button.

- **What would a first-time visitor think BaratX does?** A place to post short opinions and debate them with strangers — closest mental model is Twitter/X crossed with a daily discussion-prompt app (like a "question of the day" feature).
- **Who is it for?** Indian users who want to weigh in on current events/culture and see real replies, not just broadcast into a void.
- **What result do they expect?** Someone actually responding to their take — the tagline "Real replies — not a firehose" sets that expectation directly.
- **What confusion/doubt would remain?** Whether anyone is actually here.
